title: The Ten Commandments: God's Moral Law
summary: The Ten Commandments are the foundational moral law given by God to Moses on Mount Sinai, expressing the fundamental duties of love toward God and neighbor, and forming the core of the Church's moral teaching for living a life of holiness.

blocks.text: Introduction: The Decalogue as Divine Gift

The Ten Commandments, or Decalogue, were given by God to Moses on Mount Sinai as part of the covenant with Israel. They are not merely rules or restrictions, but a gracious gift from God showing humanity the path to life and freedom. The Commandments express the fundamental obligations of man toward God and toward his neighbor. [CCC 2055-2056]

The Church has always recognized the Decalogue as expressing the fundamental duties of man. The Ten Commandments form an organic unity in which each commandment refers to the others and to the whole; to transgress one is to break all. They illuminate the conscience of every person, revealing the fundamental vocation to love God and neighbor. [CCC 2069, 2079]
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. You shall have no other gods before me.

blocks.title: CCC 2055-2056: Gift of the Law
blocks.text: The Ten Commandments are a gracious gift from God showing the path to life and freedom, expressing fundamental obligations toward God and neighbor.
I. The Two Tables of the Law

The Ten Commandments are traditionally divided into two tables. The first three commandments concern love of God: worshiping him alone, revering his name, and keeping holy the Lord's Day. The remaining seven commandments concern love of neighbor: honoring parents, respecting life, marriage, property, truth, and purity. [CCC 2067]

Jesus summarized the whole Law and the Prophets in two commandments: love of God with all one's heart, soul, and mind, and love of neighbor as oneself. The Ten Commandments are the privileged expression of this twofold charity, showing concretely how love of God and love of neighbor are lived out. [CCC 2067]

You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it, You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments depend all the law and the prophets.

blocks.title: CCC 2067: Twofold Charity
blocks.text: The Ten Commandments express the twofold charity of love of God and love of neighbor, showing concretely how this love is lived out in daily life.
II. The First Commandment: One God Alone

The first commandment declares: I am the LORD your God; you shall have no other gods before me. This commandment calls us to faith, hope, and charity toward God. It forbids idolatry, superstition, irreligion, and atheism, calling us to worship the one true God in spirit and truth. [CCC 2084, 2110-2114]

To live the first commandment is to believe in God, to hope in him, and to love him above all things. It requires us to adore God alone, to pray to him with faith, hope, and charity, and to worship him as the source of all good. The virtue of religion disposes us to render to God the worship that is his due. [CCC 2083, 2095-2096]
Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD; and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.

blocks.title: CCC 2084: Faith, Hope, and Charity
blocks.text: The first commandment calls us to faith, hope, and charity toward God, forbidding idolatry and requiring us to adore and worship God alone.
III. The Second Commandment: Reverence for God's Name

The second commandment states: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain. The Lord's name is holy and must be treated with reverence. This commandment requires us to speak of God, the Virgin Mary, and the saints with respect and honor. [CCC 2142-2143]

The second commandment forbids blasphemy, perjury, and taking false oaths. It also prohibits the abuse of God's name to justify crimes or evil actions. We are called to bear witness to the Lord's name with humility and trust, honoring it in our speech and actions. [CCC 2148-2150, 2153]
He who blasphemes the name of the LORD shall be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him; the sojourner as well as the native, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.

blocks.title: CCC 2142-2143: Holy Name
blocks.text: The second commandment requires reverence for God's name, forbidding blasphemy, perjury, and false oaths, and calling us to honor the Lord's name in speech and action.
IV. The Third Commandment: Keep Holy the Lord's Day

The third commandment commands: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. For Christians, the Lord's Day is Sunday, the day of Christ's Resurrection. On this day, the faithful are obliged to participate in the Eucharist and to refrain from work that hinders the worship of God. [CCC 2168, 2180-2181]

Sunday is a day of grace and rest from labor, a sign of the eternal rest of heaven. It is a day for works of mercy, relaxation of mind and body, and spending time with family. The Lord's Day sanctifies the week and gives meaning to human labor by ordering it to the worship of God. [CCC 2172, 2184-2185]
Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days you shall labor, and do all your work; but the seventh day is a sabbath to the LORD your God.

blocks.title: CCC 2168: The Lord's Day
blocks.text: The third commandment calls us to keep holy the Lord's Day, Sunday, by participating in the Eucharist and resting from work that hinders worship.
V. The Fourth Commandment: Honor Your Father and Mother

The fourth commandment states: Honor your father and your mother. This commandment establishes the duties of children toward their parents and, by extension, the duties of citizens toward legitimate authorities. It promises long life and prosperity to those who keep it. [CCC 2197, 2214-2215]

The family is the original cell of social life, and the fourth commandment protects and strengthens it. Parents have the primary responsibility for the education of their children in faith, prayer, and virtue. Children owe their parents respect, gratitude, docility, and obedience, as well as material and moral support in old age. [CCC 2204, 2214-2215]

Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right. Honor your father and mother (this is the first commandment with a promise), that it may be well with you and that you may live long on the earth.

blocks.title: CCC 2197: Family and Authority
blocks.text: The fourth commandment establishes the duties of children toward parents and citizens toward authorities, protecting the family as the foundation of social life.
VI. The Fifth Commandment: Respect for Life

The fifth commandment declares: You shall not kill. Human life is sacred because it is created in God's image and entrusted to us as a stewardship. This commandment forbids murder, abortion, euthanasia, and suicide, and calls us to respect the dignity of every human person from conception to natural death. [CCC 2258, 2268-2271, 2276-2279]

The fifth commandment also requires us to care for our own health and the health of others, to avoid anger, hatred, and revenge, and to work for peace. Legitimate defense of self and others is permitted, but direct and intentional killing of an innocent person is always gravely sinful. [CCC 2263-2267, 2302-2303]
Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed; for God made man in his own image.

blocks.title: CCC 2258: Sacredness of Life
blocks.text: The fifth commandment forbids killing and calls us to respect the sacredness of human life from conception to natural death, as life is created in God's image.
VII. The Sixth and Ninth Commandments: Purity and Chastity

The sixth commandment states: You shall not commit adultery. The ninth commandment adds: You shall not covet your neighbor's wife. Together, these commandments call us to live chastity according to our state in life, respecting the dignity of marriage and the integrity of the human person. [CCC 2331, 2336, 2514-2515]

Chastity is the successful integration of sexuality within the person, leading to self-mastery and freedom. The sixth and ninth commandments forbid lust, masturbation, fornication, pornography, prostitution, rape, and homosexual acts. They call us to purity of heart, modesty, and self-control through prayer and the sacraments. [CCC 2337, 2351-2357, 2396]
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

blocks.title: CCC 2331: Chastity
blocks.text: The sixth and ninth commandments call us to live chastity according to our state in life, respecting marriage and the dignity of the human person.
VIII. The Seventh and Tenth Commandments: Justice and Detachment

The seventh commandment states: You shall not steal. The tenth commandment adds: You shall not covet your neighbor's goods. These commandments require justice and charity in the care of earthly goods, respect for private property, and detachment from disordered desire for riches. [CCC 2401, 2408, 2534-2536]

The seventh commandment forbids theft, fraud, unjust wages, and damage to others' property. It requires reparation for injustice committed and calls us to use goods responsibly, sharing with the poor. The tenth commandment forbids greed, envy, and the desire to appropriate others' goods without limit. [CCC 2401, 2408-2409, 2536]
And he said to them, Take heed, and beware of all covetousness; for a man's life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.

blocks.title: CCC 2401: Justice and Charity
blocks.text: The seventh and tenth commandments require justice and charity in caring for earthly goods, respecting property, and practicing detachment from greed.
IX. The Eighth Commandment: Truth and Witness

The eighth commandment states: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor. This commandment calls us to live in truth, to speak honestly, and to bear witness to Christ, who is the Truth. It forbids lying, perjury, rash judgment, detraction, calumny, and flattery. [CCC 2464, 2468, 2475-2477]

The eighth commandment requires respect for the truth and for the reputation of others. It calls us to practice discretion in communication, to keep confidences, and to respect privacy. Christians are called to bear witness to the Gospel in word and deed, even at the cost of their lives. [CCC 2464, 2471-2473, 2479]
Therefore, putting away falsehood, let every one speak the truth with his neighbor, for we are members one of another.

blocks.title: CCC 2464: Live in Truth
blocks.text: The eighth commandment calls us to live in truth, forbidding lying, detraction, and calumny, and requiring respect for truth and the reputation of others.
X. Living the Commandments in Christ

The Ten Commandments are not merely external rules but an expression of the new life we receive in Baptism. Christ did not abolish the Law but fulfilled it, giving us the grace to live it through the Holy Spirit. The Commandments are a path to freedom, showing us how to love God and neighbor as Christ loved us. [CCC 2074, 2082]

To keep the Commandments is to remain in Christ's love. Through prayer, the sacraments, and the practice of virtue, we grow in our ability to live the moral law with joy and freedom. The Commandments are not a burden but a light for our path, guiding us to eternal life with God. [CCC 2075, 2083]
If you keep my commandments, you will abide in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and abide in his love.

blocks.title: CCC 2074-2075: Life in Christ
blocks.text: The Commandments express the new life received in Baptism; Christ fulfilled the Law and gives us grace to live it through the Holy Spirit.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer: Prayer for Fidelity to the Commandments
blocks.text: O Lord God, you have given us the Ten Commandments as a path to life and freedom. Grant us the grace to know your law, the strength to keep it, and the love to fulfill it with joy. Help us to love you above all things and to love our neighbor as ourselves, through Christ our Lord. Amen.
